column1: The control of fire was the first and perhaps greatest of humanity’s steps towards a life-enhancing technology.
column2: 人类对火的掌控，是迈向提升生活质量的首个也是可能最伟大的技术突破。

column1: To early man, fire was a divine gift randomly delivered in the form of lightning, forest fire or burning lava.
column2: 对早期人类而言，火是神赐的礼物，以闪电、森林大火或熔岩的形式随机降临。

column1: Unable to make flame for themselves, the earliest peoples probably stored fire by keeping slow burning logs alight or by carrying charcoal in pots.
column2: 由于无法自行生火，最早的人类可能通过保存缓慢燃烧的木柴或携带装在容器中的木炭来储存火种。

column1: How and where man learnt how to produce flame at will is unknown.
column2: 人类如何以及在何处学会随意制造火焰至今仍不清楚。

column1: It was probably a secondary invention, accidentally made during tool-making operations with wood or stone.
column2: 这可能是一种次要的发明，是在使用木头或石头进行工具制造的过程中偶然产生的。

column1: Studies of primitive societies suggest that the earliest method of making fire was through friction.
column2: 对原始社会的研究表明，人们最早通过摩擦来生火。

column1: European peasants would insert a wooden drill in a round hole and rotate it briskly between their palms.
column2: 欧洲的农民会将一个木制钻头插入圆形孔洞中，然后快速地在双手之间旋转该钻头。

column1: This process could be speeded up by wrapping a cord around the drill and pulling on each end.
column2: 可以通过在钻头周围缠绕一根绳子，然后分别拉扯绳子的两端来加速这一过程。

column1: The Ancient Greeks used lenses or concave mirrors to concentrate the sun’s rays and burning glasses were also used by Mexican Aztecs and the Chinese.
column2: 古希腊人使用透镜或凹面镜来集中阳光；墨西哥阿兹特克人和中国人也使用了燃烧玻璃来利用阳光。

column1: Percussion methods of fire-lighting date back to Paleolithic times, when some Stone Age tool-makers discovered that chipping flints produced sparks.
column2: 敲打取火的方法可追溯到旧石器时代，当时一些史前工具制造者发现，敲击燧石会产生火花。

column1: The technique became more efficient after the discovery of iron, about 5000 years ago In Arctic North America, the Eskimos produced a slow-burning spark by striking quartz against iron pyrites, a compound that contains sulphur.
column2: 大约5000年前，随着铁的发现，这项取火技术变得更加高效。在北极北美的因纽特人通过将石英击打在黄铁矿上（一种含硫的化合物），产生了一种缓慢燃烧的火花。

column1: The Chinese lit their fires by striking porcelain with bamboo.
column2: 中国人通过用竹子敲击瓷器来点燃火种。

column1: In Europe, the combination of steel, flint and tinder remained the main method of fire-lighting until the mid 19th century.
column2: 在欧洲，直到19世纪中期，钢、打火石和火绒的组合仍然是点火的主要方法。

column1: Fire-lighting was revolutionized by the discovery of phosphorus, isolated in 1669 by a German alchemist trying to transmute silver into gold.
column2: 点火技术因磷的发现而发生革命性变革。1669年，一位德国炼金术士在尝试将银转化为黄金的过程中，发现了磷元素。

column1: Impressed by the element’s combustibility, several 17th century chemists used it to manufacture fire-lighting devices, but the results were dangerously inflammable.
column2: 受到磷可燃性的启发，17世纪几位化学家尝试用它制造点火装置，但结果却极易燃烧，存在严重安全隐患。

column1: With phosphorus costing the equivalent of several hundred pounds per ounce, the first matches were expensive.
column2: 由于磷的价格高达每盎司数百英镑，最初的火柴因此十分昂贵。

column1: The first matches resembling those used today were made in 1827 by John Walker, an English pharmacist who borrowed the formula from a military rocket-maker called Congreve.
column2: 最早类似今天火柴的火柴出现在1827年，由英国药剂师约翰·沃克制成，他从一位军事火箭制造者康格雷夫那里借鉴了配方。

column1: Walker never patented his invention, and three years later it was copied by a Samuel Jones, who marketed his product as Lucifers.
column2: 沃克从未为他的发明申请过专利。三年后，塞缪尔·琼斯复制了这项发明，并将其命名为‘Lucifers’。

column1: However, since white phosphorus is a deadly poison, from 1845 match-makers exposed to its fumes succumbed to necrosis, a disease that eats away jaw-bones.
column2: 然而，由于白磷是一种致命毒物，从1845年起，接触其烟雾的火柴制造工人因坏死而死于颌骨侵蚀。

column1: It wasn’t until 1906 that the substance was eventually banned.
column2: 直到1906年，这种物质才被正式禁止使用。

column1: That was 62 years after a Swedish chemist called Pasch had discovered non-toxic red or amorphous phosphorus, a development exploited commercially by Pasch’s compatriot J E Lundstrom in 1885.
column2: 那是在一位名叫帕施的瑞典化学家发现无毒的红色或无定形磷元素之后62年才发生的。这一发现后来被帕施的同胞J.E.伦德斯特罗姆在1885年商业化应用了。

column1: America lagged behind Europe in match technology and safety standards.
column2: 在美国火柴技术和安全标准方面，美国落后于欧洲。

column1: It wasn’t until 1900 that the Diamond Match Company bought a French patent for safety matches — but the formula did not work properly in the different climatic conditions prevailing in America and it was another 11 years before scientists finally adapted the French patent for the US.
column2: 直到1900年，Diamond Match公司才购得一项法国安全火柴专利，但该配方在美国不同的气候条件下无法正常运作，直到11年后科学家们才最终将其适应于美国的气候条件。

column1: The Americans, however, can claim several “firsts” in match technology and marketing.
column2: 然而，美国人可以在火柴技术和营销领域宣称多项‘首次’成就。

column1: In 1892 the Diamond Match Company pioneered book matches.
column2: 1892年，钻石火柴公司首创了书火柴。

column1: The innovation didn’t catch on until after 1896, when a brewery had the novel idea of advertising its product in match books.
column2: 这一创新直到1896年之后才普及。当时有一家啤酒厂想到了一个新奇的想法：在火柴书上宣传自己的产品。

column1: Today book matches are the most widely used type in the US, with 90 percent handed out free by hotels, restaurants and others.
column2: 如今，在美国，90%的书火柴由酒店、餐馆等场所免费分发。

column1: Other American innovations include an anti-afterglow solution to prevent the match from smoldering after it has been blown out; and the waterproof match, which lights after eight hours in water.
column2: 其他美国的创新还包括一种防止火柴熄灭后继续燃烧的防余烬方案；以及一种防水火柴，能在水中浸泡八小时后点燃。
